newsitem.title: UK: Grobbelaar is great keeper, says commentator Wilson.
newsitem.headline: Grobbelaar is great keeper, says commentator Wilson.

text.p: Former Scottish goalkeeper Bob Wilson, now one of Britain's top sports commentators, said on Tuesday that Bruce Grobbelaar, on trial over match-fixing allegations, was a great keeper.
Wilson told a court in this southern English town that the range of Grobbelaar's keeping when he played with Liverpool was "the outstanding aspect" of his game.
Wilson praised Grobbelaar as an unorthodox star who was prepared to leave the penalty area and act as an extra defender.

"The problem with it was, when he got the decision wrong, they were spectacularly wrong and he was yards away from his charge, which was the goal." Grobbelaar is accused with former Wimbledon keeper Hans Segers, ex-Wimbledon and Aston Villa striker John Fashanu and Malaysian businessman Heng Suan Lim of rigging games to benefit an Asian betting syndicate.
All four defendants deny the charges although both keepers admit they were paid in cash by Lim for providing match forecasts.
Wilson told the court he had devoted a chapter to Grobbelaar in his book on goalkeepers entitled: "You have got to be crazy."
"I felt it was necessary to include Bruce. He was still at Liverpool at the time but such was his impression on me and other goalkeepers.
"If there is one football club where you are not allowed to be anything other than truly consistent, it is Liverpool Football Club," he told the court.
During his 13 years at Liverpool, Grobbelaar won five league titles and became English club soccer's most successful goalkeeper.
Grobbelaar told the trial on Monday he had been drunk when a video showing him allegedly discussing fixing soccer matches was secretly shot.
